disposition_reason: Primary apiary-sampling study reporting Pb, Cd and Ni concentrations (mg/kg) in honey composites from three districts of Kellem Wollega Zone, Ethiopia, measured by ICP-OES.
disposition_locator: Table 4 p. 7; Table 5 p. 10; Sections 2.2 and 2.5 pp. 3–4

study.design: apiary sampling (cluster design; composited) with USEPA-style health risk assessment
study.material_scope: Honey (Apis mellifera) from apiary points in three districts; floral/botanical type not reported
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Growing origin: Dambi Dollo, Gawo Kebe and Anafilo (Anfillo) districts, Kellem Wollega Zone, Oromia, Ethiopia; collected at apiary points (not purchased). Text once refers to 'Dembi Dollo Market honey' (p. 8, p. 9), which conflicts with the apiary-point description in Section 2.2.
study.sampling_unit: composite honey samples (each pooling 5 apiary-point subsamples; 15 subsamples total), each measured in triplicate
study.method: Wet acid digestion (0.5 g honey, 2 mL HNO3 + 1.5 mL HClO4, Kjeldahl block 160–240 °C under reflux, 2 h 45 min), filtered, made to 100 mL, diluted 1:10, ICP-OES (PerkinElmer Optima 8000)
study.lod_loq: Table 2 (mg/L, solution basis): Pb IDL 0.469, MDL 0.582, LOQ 1.576; Cd IDL 0.099, MDL 0.128, LOQ 0.327; Ni IDL 0.028, MDL 0.043, LOQ 0.114 (also Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn). No honey-basis (mg/kg) LOD/LOQ given.
study.basis: mg/kg honey as sampled (0.5 g honey digested); source does not state 'fresh' or 'wet weight' explicitly
study.qa: Spike recovery on honey (Table 3): Pb 114.82%, Cd 92.27%, Ni 97.14% (overall 89.09–114.82%); replicate RSD 0.12–1.35% (Table 3 column shows up to 1.70% for Cu); matrix-matched calibration 0.05–5.05 mg/L, R² 0.995–0.999. No CRM reported.

findings.material: honey (Apis mellifera; floral type not reported)
findings.censoring: No non-detects reported; all values printed as quantified means.
findings.locator: Table 4, Pb row, column 'Dambi Dollo'; p. 7
findings.notes: n=1 composite sample per district (5 apiary-point subsamples pooled; Section 2.2 p. 3). The mean ± SD is over 3 replicate measurements of that one composite (Table 4 footnote 'n = Number of replicate measurements'), so SD reflects analytical repeatability, not between-sample variability. District is within Kellem Wollega Zone, Oromia, Ethiopia (growing origin = sampling district). Pb did not differ significantly among sites (NS, p > 0.05, one-way ANOVA). Source detection limits are given only in mg/L of measured solution (Table 2, p. 5); they are not converted to µg/kg here. Per the stated prep (0.5 g honey to 100 mL, then 1:10 dilution before ICP-OES), the stated MDL would correspond to roughly 200–2000 × MDL mg/kg honey depending on whether the 1:10 dilution applies — for Pb and Cd above the reported honey concentration in either case, and for Ni at or above it; see unresolved.

controls.control: Siting: transfer hives away from polluted hotspots; stricter controls on agricultural and industrial emissions near apiaries
controls.comparator: None measured; authors attribute peak Pb at Anafilo to the area's gold mining industry
controls.outcome: Recommendation only. Pb did not differ significantly among the three districts (p > 0.05), so the mining attribution is not supported by a statistical contrast in this dataset.

controls.control: Use food-grade storage containers (unsuitable containers can leach heavy metals)
controls.outcome: Recommendation only; container leaching proposed as a contributing source, not tested.

controls.control: Honey pretreatment before sale; routine monitoring and source identification

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Summary calls the values 'mg/kg wet weight'; the paper reports mg/kg of honey as sampled and never uses 'wet weight'.
Summary describes the region as 'African artisanal-mining-impacted'; the paper says 'intensive gold mining industry' (p. 9) and does not use 'artisanal'.

Summary states Dambi Dollo and Gawo Kebe 'fall in the NYSDOH high risk category'; the paper's abstract describes the risk as 'potential moderate lifetime carcinogenic risk' — the 'high' categorization is the summary's own inference from the category table (p. 13).
Summary lists HNO3 as 65–68%; the paper gives both 69–72% (Section 2.3) and 65–68% (Section 2.5.1).

Summary presents the detection-limit table and the 18–21 mg/kg Pb results without noting that, by the paper's own sample mass and dilution, the reported honey concentrations fall below the stated solution-basis MDL/LOQ.
Summary treats the EU 2023/915 Cd limit of 0.05 mg/kg for honey as established; that limit is the paper's citation (p. 8) and was not verified against the regulation in this pass.
unresolved: Internal plausibility: Table 2 gives Pb MDL 0.582 mg/L and LOQ 1.576 mg/L (solution). With 0.5 g honey made to 100 mL (and a further 1:10 dilution), 21.42 mg/kg Pb corresponds to ~0.107 mg/L in the digest (~0.011 mg/L after 1:10) — below the stated MDL/LOQ. Same holds for Cd (~0.0115 mg/L vs MDL 0.128) and Ni (~0.044 mg/L vs MDL 0.043, before the 1:10 dilution). Either the limits are expressed on another basis or the reported concentrations are not quantifiable as described. Cannot resolve from the text.
Table 3 spike levels (Pb 700 mg/kg, Ni 290 mg/kg, Cd 200 mg/kg added) are 30–150× the native concentration; recoveries at these levels do not demonstrate accuracy near the reported concentrations.
Floral/botanical type of honey is not reported.
Paper refers to 'Dembi Dollo Market' honey twice (pp. 8–9) while Section 2.2 describes apiary-point sampling; purchase vs apiary origin for the Dambi Dollo composite is therefore slightly ambiguous.
Cu, Fe, Mn and Zn were also measured (Table 4) but are outside the HMI analyte list and are not extracted as findings.
